name: Anterior approach to the cervicothoracic junction
corridor: Incision along the medial sternocleidomastoid to the sternal notch, same retropharyngeal plane as anterior cervical, with optional manubriotomy or 3 cm medial clavicle resection to reach T1–T2

positioning.text: Position so a nasogastric tube is in place and a lateral radiograph or sagittal CT can show whether the manubrial notch already sees the upper thoracic spine.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial sternocleidomastoid, sternal notch, and manubrium. A left-sided approach puts the thoracic duct at risk; a right-sided approach is more likely to injure the recurrent laryngeal nerve.

incision.text: Start along the medial sternocleidomastoid down to the sternal notch and continue onto the proximal third of the sternum if a manubrial window is needed.

superficial_interval.text: Divide platysma, then deep cervical fascia along the anteromedial sternocleidomastoid. Release the superficial fascia fully. The omohyoid at C6, and sternohyoid/sternothyroid, may be divided to improve the extensile window.

deep_interval.text: Stay medial to the carotid sheath and bluntly develop the plane to prevertebral fascia. If the manubrial notch already sees the upper thoracic vertebra, a standard lower-cervical window may suffice. Otherwise open the manubrium or the sternoclavicular joint and resect about 3 cm of medial clavicle (usable as strut graft). Mobilize the brachiocephalic trunk as needed, protect lung with a sponge, open prevertebral fascia, confirm the level, and mobilize longus colli.

layers.text: Skin, platysma, strap muscles, carotid-sheath versus visceral plane, optional manubrium/clavicle, prevertebral fascia, then C7–T2.

structures_at_risk.text: The esophagus, carotid, recurrent laryngeal nerve, thoracic duct (left), brachiocephalic trunk, and lung are at risk.

danger_zones.text: A formal sternotomy for levels below T2 has more morbidity than posterolateral alternatives. Unrecognized esophageal injury is potentially lethal.

retraction_hazards.text: Use blunt dissection only between the sheath and viscera. Hold carotid bleeding with direct pressure and call vascular surgery.

exposure.text: Shows anterior C7–T1 through T1–T2; lower levels may be reachable depending on sternal anatomy.

limitations.text: If the manubrial notch does not see the target on sagittal imaging, a manubrial or sternoclavicular extension is required. Below T2, posterolateral windows are usually easier.

indications.text: Used for anterior decompression or reconstruction of the injured C7–T2 column.

closure.text: Approximate split muscles, suture transected straps and platysma, close skin, and place a drain through a separate stab.

complications.text: Complications include esophageal perforation, thoracic-duct leak, recurrent-laryngeal palsy, carotid or brachiocephalic injury, and lung injury.

procedure_applications.condition: Anterior C7–T2 decompression or reconstruction is done through a cervical incision, extended with a manubrial window when the sternum hides the target

questions.question: How do you decide whether a standard lower-cervical cut reaches the CTJ?
questions.answer: If looking through the manubrial notch on a lateral radiograph or sagittal CT you can see the upper thoracic vertebra, a common lower-cervical window may suffice; otherwise extend.

questions.question: How much medial clavicle may be resected, and for what?
questions.answer: About 3 cm, which can be used as a strut graft.

questions.question: Which side risks the thoracic duct?
